name: Nilathingal Thundathan Perumal Shrine (Thiru Nilathingal Thundam), Kanchipuram
nativeName: நிலாத்திங்கள் துண்டப் பெருமாள் கோயில் (திருநிலாத்திங்கள் துண்டம்), காஞ்சிபுரம்
deity: Vishnu as Nilathingal Thundathan Perumal, "the Lord of the moonlight piece" — the Divya Desam of Thiru Nilathingal Thundam, a Vishnu shrine within the Shaiva Ekambareswarar Temple
period: A Divya Desam of Thondai Nadu, sung by Thirumangai Alvar in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham
summary: Thiru Nilathingal Thundam is a small Vishnu shrine inside Kanchipuram's great Shaiva Ekambareswarar Temple, a Divya Desam sung by Thirumangai Alvar, where the Lord is the guardian of the Moon's cool light.

sections.history: Thiru Nilathingal Thundam is not a separate temple but a Vishnu shrine inside the Ekambareswarar Temple of Kanchipuram, the Shaiva temple of the earth element among the Pancha Bhoota Sthalams. It is one of the 108 Divya Desams of Thondai Nadu, sung by Thirumangai Alvar in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham, with one pasuram credited to it. The shrine lies in the first precinct around the main sanctum, to the south-west. Its Vishnu stands within a temple whose eleven-tiered rayagopuram was raised under the Vijayanagara king Krishnadevaraya in 1509. That a Divya Desam sits inside a Shiva temple is a mark of the old Kanchi, where Shaiva and Vaishnava devotion share the same ground.
sections.architecture: The shrine is a modest sanctum set in the first prakaram of the Ekambareswarar complex, under the Purusha Sukta Vimanam, with the Chandra Pushkarini as its sacred tank. There is no separate shrine for the Goddess, who is named Nilathingal Thunda Nayagi, and no separate festival image: the shrine is a quiet one within the grand temple, whose towering gopuram and pillared halls surround it.
sections.legends: The name means the Lord of the moonlight piece, and is linked with the cool rays of the Moon. One tradition tells that Parvati performed penance at Kanchi to win Shiva; Vishnu is said to have taken the crescent from Shiva's head and let its cool rays fall upon the mango tree and upon Parvati, easing her austerity. Another telling has Vishnu shielding her sand lingam from the flood of the Ganga. In either account the Lord of Nilathingal Thundam is the gentle helper of the goddess's devotion.
sections.festivals: The shrine is observed within the calendar of the Ekambareswarar Temple, whose great festival is the Panguni Uthiram Brahmotsavam; the Vaishnava days of Vaikunta Ekadashi and the Margazhi recitations are honoured here as well. Confirm dates locally.
sections.experience: Come to Ekambareswarar first, and walk the first precinct to the south-west to find the small Vishnu sanctum, a rare Divya Desam inside a Shiva temple. Ask the priests to point the way. Pause at this meeting of two traditions, then continue to the nearby Vaishnava Divya Desams of Kanchipuram to complete the pilgrimage.

visit.timings: The shrine opens with the Ekambareswarar Temple: morning and evening sessions with a midday closure. Confirm current timings locally before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctums; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: This is a shrine inside the Ekambareswarar Temple in Kanchipuram; enter by the great rayagopuram and ask for the Nilathingal Thundam sanctum in the first precinct. Chennai, about 70 km to the north-east, is the nearest major airport, and Kanchipuram town is the nearest railhead.
